title: Frontend vs Backend Boundaries
definition: Frontend development encompasses all presentation, interaction, accessibility, and client-side logic executing inside user agents (browsers), distinct from server-side storage and business processing.

title: Web Platform Foundations (HTML, CSS, JS)
definition: The separation of concerns between structure/meaning (HTML), visual styling/layout (CSS), and client runtime behavior (JavaScript).

title: Web Platform & Client-Server Architecture
definition: The distributed network architecture of the web where client user agents request, parse, render, and execute static and dynamic web assets hosted on remote servers.

title: Client-Server Split & Browser Runtime
definition: The clear structural separation between client-side execution (browser rendering engine, DOM, JavaScript runtime) and server-side processing (databases, server APIs, persistent storage).

title: The Frontend Triad (HTML, CSS, JavaScript Roles)
definition: The three foundational pillars of frontend engineering: HTML defines semantics and document structure, CSS defines visual styling and layout, and JavaScript defines interactive runtime behavior.

title: HTML Elements, Tags & Attributes
definition: HTML elements represent distinct document nodes consisting of an opening tag, optional attributes providing metadata, content, and a closing tag.

title: HTML Element Anatomy
definition: The syntactic structure of an HTML element, consisting of an opening tag with element name and optional attributes, inner text or child node content, and a closing tag.

title: Opening vs Closing Tags & Void Elements
definition: Opening tags begin an element and house attributes; closing tags finalize container elements with a forward slash. Void elements (such as and ) cannot have content and never have closing tags.

title: HTML Attributes & Key-Value Configuration
definition: Name-value pairs placed inside an element's opening tag that modify behavior, provide metadata, link external resources, or assign styling classes and identifiers.

title: Document Tree Hierarchy & Element Nesting
definition: The recursive parent-child tree structure of the Document Object Model (DOM) requiring elements to close in the reverse order of opening without improper cross-boundary overlapping.

title: CSS Box Model
definition: The rectangular box geometry encompassing every rendered DOM element, consisting of content, padding, border, and margin areas.

title: CSS Flexible Box Layout (Flexbox)
definition: A 1-dimensional layout model providing directional alignment, distribution of space, and flexible item sizing along main and cross axes.

title: Flex Container Formatting Context
definition: An element with display: flex applied that establishes a flex formatting context, transforming its immediate direct children into flex items.

title: Flex Items & Flow Behavior
definition: The immediate direct child elements of a flex container that participate in flex layout calculations, alignment, and distribution.

title: Main vs Cross Axis Dynamics
definition: The two perpendicular axes established by flex-direction: the main axis along which items flow and justify-content operates, and the cross axis along which align-items operates.

title: Flex Space Distribution & Alignment
definition: The use of justify-content (main axis distribution) and align-items (cross axis alignment) along with the gap property to space and align flex items without hardcoded margins.

title: JavaScript Functions & Execution Scope
definition: First-class callable objects in JavaScript that encapsulate reusable computation, create local variable scope, and can be passed as values or returned from other functions.

title: Function Return Values & Output Channels
definition: The explicit data value delivered back to the caller of a function via the return statement, which terminates function execution immediately.

title: console.log vs Return Values
definition: console.log() is an I/O side effect intended for developer diagnostic inspection in DevTools; it does not supply data back to the calling expression or assign values to variables.

title: Call Expression Value Substitution
definition: When a function finishes execution, its call expression in code (e.g. calculateTotal(10, 2)) is evaluated and substituted with the function's returned value.

title: Implicit undefined Return Behavior
definition: In JavaScript, any function that finishes executing without encountering an explicit return statement with a value implicitly returns undefined.

title: Systematic Frontend Debugging
definition: A disciplined, hypothesis-driven workflow for diagnosing defects using browser DevTools, console logs, breakpoint inspection, and DOM state verification.

title: Syntax Errors vs Runtime Exceptions vs Logic Bugs
definition: Syntax errors prevent code parsing; runtime exceptions halt execution during runtime (e.g. TypeError); logic bugs allow code to run but produce incorrect visual or behavioral results.

title: DOM Element Query Resolution & Null Checking
definition: Resolving DOM nodes with document.querySelector; if a selector matches no element, it returns null, causing downstream property access or listener attachments to throw runtime TypeErrors.

title: Event Listener Binding & Handler Lifecycle
definition: Registering callback functions to user interaction events (click, submit, input) on valid DOM element references so user actions trigger state and UI updates.

title: CSS Selector & Property Invalidation
definition: Browsers silently discard invalid CSS property names, misspelled values, or mismatched selectors without throwing JavaScript console errors, requiring computed style DevTools inspection.

title: JavaScript Browser Runtime & Script Execution
definition: The browser execution environment where JavaScript executes in a single-threaded event loop, interacts with host Web APIs, and mutates live DOM nodes.

title: The DOM as JavaScript's Live Document Interface
definition: The object-oriented tree representation of the rendered HTML document exposed to JavaScript via the document object to inspect and mutate nodes in real time.

title: Event-Driven UI Programming
definition: The architectural pattern where JavaScript code registers listener callbacks that execute asynchronously in response to user actions like clicks, keyboard input, or form submissions.

title: Variable Declarations: let vs const
definition: Modern block-scoped variable keywords: const creates an immutable identifier binding that cannot be reassigned; let allows reassigning values over time.

title: Variable Reassignment & Identifier Scope
definition: Updating the value associated with an existing let variable identifier in memory during script execution, distinct from re-declaring the variable.

title: JavaScript Primitive Types
definition: The foundational immutable data types in JavaScript: string, number, boolean, undefined, null, symbol, and bigint.

title: Strict Equality (===) vs Loose Equality (==)
definition: The strict comparison operator (===) that verifies both value and type without coercion, unlike loose equality (==) which performs unpredictable automatic type conversion.

title: JavaScript Type Coercion Rules
definition: The automatic or explicit conversion of values from one data type to another (e.g. String(42), Number('10'), or implicit string concatenation with +).

title: Conditional Branching (if, else if, else)
definition: Control flow structures that evaluate boolean expressions to choose between divergent execution paths in code.

title: Truthy and Falsy Value Evaluation
definition: The boolean coercion of non-boolean values in conditional contexts: false, 0, '', null, undefined, and NaN are falsy; all other values (including [] and {}) are truthy.

title: Logical Operators & Short-Circuit Evaluation
definition: Logical AND (&&), OR (||), and NOT (!) operators that combine conditions and short-circuit evaluation as soon as the outcome is determined.

title: Loop Iteration Bounds & Control Lifecycle
definition: The standard loop mechanism (for, while) defining initialization, exit condition test, and step increment to execute a code block repeatedly.

title: The Accumulator Pattern
definition: Initializing a variable before a loop and incrementally updating it during each iteration to compute sums, aggregates, filtered collections, or transformed outputs.

title: Loop Termination & Infinite Loop Prevention
definition: Ensuring the loop condition advances toward falsy on every iteration so execution terminates safely without freezing the browser thread.

title: Arrays as Ordered Collections
definition: Sequential list data structures in JavaScript that store ordered collections of any data type, accessible by numerical zero-based index.

title: Zero-Indexed Array Access & Array Length
definition: Reading and updating array elements where indices start at 0 and end at array.length - 1; accessing out-of-bounds indices returns undefined.

title: Array Transformation & Iteration Methods
definition: Standard array prototype methods including push, pop, slice, map, and filter that manipulate collection contents imperatively or immutably.

title: JavaScript Objects & Key-Value Modeling
definition: Unordered dictionary structures that model entities using named string properties mapped to arbitrary values, functions, or nested objects.

title: Dot vs Bracket Property Access
definition: Accessing object properties using literal identifiers (obj.property) versus dynamic string evaluation (obj[variableOrExpression]).

title: Nested Data Modeling with Objects & Arrays
definition: Composing complex domain data models by nesting objects within arrays and arrays within objects, accessed via chained property and index lookups.

title: Composite JavaScript Program Synthesis
definition: Integrating variables, conditional logic, loops, modular functions, and structured data models into a unified, responsive client-side application.
